style: 3D animated (Pixar-style CG) for 0-39.37 s; hard cut into a 3.7 s live-action handheld phone flex tag (39.37-43.03 s) under a 'HORSEPOWER >' caption, ending on 'CREATE VIDS IN BIO'. Yellow bold italic word-by-word captions with dark shadow, centred around 55-60% of frame height; white serif title cards ('PREVIOUSLY...', '2 YEARS LATER...').
logline: Nate proposes under the Eiffel Tower and is publicly turned down for a rich older man; he grinds at his laptop for two years, and when the couple pull up next to him at a Paris red light he is in a purple hypercar with his own jet overhead - she begs him to take her back and he sings 'La la la, I can't hear you' and drives off in a blast of exhaust flame.

hook.mechanic: Cold open at the moment of rejection: kneeling proposal at the Eiffel Tower with a crowd filming on phones, she leans in and shouts 'Hell no!'; cut to his close-up holding the ring box at the lens as his face falls; she walks off, a whip-pan lands on a rich older man's gold watch and she says 'I told you I like older men!'. Humiliation, rival and motive in 7 s.

montage.description: Wordless grind montage (1.4 s, 9 shots, median 0.16 s): the same locked-off frontal shot of Nate at his laptop in his bedroom, flickering between night (lit only by the cold blue screen) and day (warm window light) every 3-10 frames - a time-lapse made of match cuts. His expression stays hard and focused; it ends on a 3-frame punch-in, then cuts to him in a black suit in a sunset penthouse. Note: the laptop screen is never shown - the work is implied, not displayed. For fomo this is the slot for real trading screens.

stats.dead_air: No silent dead air: music runs throughout; one deliberate near-silence drop of ~0.3 s at 28.6-28.8 s right before she spots Nate ('Wha-... Nate?!'). Gaps with no dialogue: 0.80-4.60 (3.8 s, rejection reaction + walk-off), 6.00-8.09 (2.1 s, Rolls-Royce insert), 9.03-11.05 (2.0 s), 15.12-29.15 (14.0 s, the transformation: empty plaza, montage, penthouse, '2 YEARS LATER', boulevard), 30.54-34.92 (4.4 s, Nate smiles, points, jet flies over), 39.00-43.03 (4.0 s, live-action tag).

beats.summary: HOOK: proposal at the Eiffel Tower, crowd filming; she shouts 'Hell no!'. Close-up: Nate holding the ring box, face falling. She turns and walks away.
The rival: whip-pan to an older man's gold watch; she hugs his arm - 'I told you I like older men!'. Rolls-Royce grille. At the car door: 'This is what I wanted.' She gets in, the car drives away.
The wound: push-in on Nate alone ('Just Paris with you.') to an extreme close-up of his eye and a tear; flashback 'PREVIOUSLY...': she cups his face - 'I love you, Nate. I'll never leave you.'
Turn: plaza now empty, sun flaring behind him; he looks at the ring, puts it away, and his face hardens into a frown.
MONTAGE: day/night flicker of Nate working at his laptop in a small bedroom.
Arrival: black suit in a sunset penthouse, checks his watch, smirks; camera drifts past him to the skyline and fades to black under '2 YEARS LATER...'.

Reversal: Paris boulevard at dusk, a purple hypercar beside the couple's Rolls-Royce at a red light. She looks over - 'Wha-... Nate?!' He smiles, points to the sky: a jet with 'NATE' on the side flies over.
Payoff: she opens the door and leans out - 'Nate, please take me back. I shouldn't have left you.' He sings 'La la la, I can't hear you!' and launches off, exhaust spitting flames past her.
Real-life tag: rapid live-action handheld flexes under 'HORSEPOWER >', ending on 'CREATE VIDS IN BIO'.

transcription: faster-whisper 'small' (CPU, int8). The first full pass (16 words from 5.0 s) missed most lines, so it was re-run on short windows (0-2.2, 10.3-13, 12.8-16.2, 16-26, 26-39.4 s) and every line checked against the burned-in word-by-word captions. Whisper also hallucinated 'The blue...' (15.1-16.2) and 'Thank you for watching!' (23-26) over music; both dropped.
why_it_works: The hook is a universal nightmare at peak stakes: a public proposal, a crowd filming, and a shouted 'Hell no!' in the first second.
The rival is introduced by objects before faces - a gold watch, then a Rolls-Royce grille - so 'money over love' reads instantly without exposition.
The wound is held, not told: one long push-in from a medium shot to a tear in his eye, then a soft-focus 'PREVIOUSLY...' memory of 'I'll never leave you' that makes the betrayal sting.
The turn is purely visual: the crowd vanishes, the sun flares behind him and his face hardens in a held push-in - a clean 'decision' beat with no words.
The grind montage is tiny (1.4 s) but legible: one locked-off frame flickering day/night says 'years of work' through match cuts. It is the exact slot where a brand can put its product screen.
Mirrored staging makes the payoff land: Paris and a Rolls-Royce in both halves, but now he is in the bigger car, at eye level with her, and she is the one behind glass.
Escalating flex beats inside the payoff - hypercar, smile, point to the sky, 'NATE' jet, 'NATE' plate, exhaust flames - each one a separate 1-3 s shot, joined by whips.
The comeback is playful, not angry ('La la la, I can't hear you!'), which makes it shareable and quotable.
Music carries the 14 s wordless middle and builds into the live-action tag, where a bass-heavy drop and 0.1-0.2 s cuts make the creator's real life feel like the sequel.
The tag ends on an on-screen CTA ('CREATE VIDS IN BIO') that matches the caption CTA, turning the story's flex into a funnel.
undetermined: Music not identified and not heard; all music/sound notes come from loudness, frequency and onset measurements. Whether the sub-bass swells are engine SFX or musical bass hits cannot be confirmed.
'Just Paris with you.' - speaker unclear: Nate's mouth barely moves; it may be his whisper or her voice as a memory leading into the flashback.
The 'I told you I like older men!' timing (4.60-6.00) is taken from the captions; whisper's word times were squeezed.
The 2.17-7.02 auto shot is split at 3.40 where a whip-pan hides the change from the wide to the watch close-up; it could also be one continuous whip move generated in one clip.
The laptop screen in the montage is never shown, so there is no reference here for how trading screens are framed.
The live-action tag cuts are 0.07-0.4 s and several are hidden in whip blur; 14 shots is a careful count but may be off by one or two.

tag.description: Live-action 'real me' flex tag, 14 handheld phone shots in 3.7 s (median ~0.13 s), mostly joined by motion-blur whips: car selfie, sneaker/clothes room with purple LED, night selfie with friends by a car, yacht at sea, jet-ski POV at sunset, pool blur, walking past a private jet and black cars, purple-lit van lounge, driving a luxury car at night, pink-lit living room, diamond watch, arms raised on a high balcony, red supercars in a garage. Caption 'HORSEPOWER >' with a small animated pixel-art pickaxe sticker, switching to 'CREATE VIDS IN BIO' + fire emoji for the last 0.6 s [do not copy]. Music hits hardest here (loudest, most sub-bass, busiest transients).

sound: Correction to the brief: the reel is not almost wordless. Whisper's first pass caught 16 words starting at 5 s; a re-run on short windows plus the burned-in captions gives 45 words in 11 lines, starting with the shouted 'Hell no!' at 0.0 s. Still, it is music-driven: speech covers only ~25% of runtime and the whole 14 s transformation (15-29 s) has no words at all.

Music (measured, not heard - no listening possible): one continuous bed with a dark, warm tone (spectral centroid ~0.9-1.3 kHz for 2-30 s, low high-frequency energy) and very few sharp transients 4-32 s (2-6 onsets per 4 s) - i.e. sustained, pad/melody-led, not a hard drum grid, under the heartbreak and the grind.

Energy builds as the payback arrives: from ~32 s (jet reveal) the track gets brighter (centroid ~1.8-1.9 kHz) and busier (9 onsets per 4 s), and at the live-action tag (39.4 s) it peaks - about +4 dB louder, sub-bass up ~10 dB, 19-29 onsets per 4 s, centroid 2.7 kHz: a drop timed to the cut into real footage.

Sub-bass swells (likely engine rumble / bass hits; cannot confirm by ear) sit under the money beats: the Rolls-Royce grille and walk-off (6.0-6.8 s), the car pulling away (10.0-10.8 s), the penthouse reveal (21.25 s), the jet (32.8-33.0 s), the exhaust flames (38.75-39.4 s).
A ~0.3 s near-silence at 28.6-28.8 s drops the music out just before she recognises him - the one 'beat of silence' in the reel, used for the reveal.

What carries the story without dialogue: props as status markers (ring box, gold watch, Rolls-Royce grille, black suit, silver watch check, 'NATE' jet livery, 'NATE' number plate, exhaust flames), expression changes held in long push-ins (hope -> shock -> tear -> hardened frown), the empty plaza (the crowd is gone = he is alone), the day/night laptop flicker (time passing = grind), and mirrored staging (Paris + Rolls-Royce in both halves, but now he is the one in the bigger car).
Nate's last line is sung ('La la la, I can't hear you!'), playful and mocking, laughing at the wheel - the payoff is tone, not a speech.
method: Auto cut list (frame-difference) checked with 0.1 s frame strips over the whole reel and per-frame differences around doubtful spots. 40 auto shots -> 41: added cuts hidden by a whip-pan (3.40), a car-body wipe (10.55) and a whip at 29.50; folded a 3-frame punch-in (21.20) into the last montage shot; merged motion-blur false cuts in the live-action tag (39.77-40.68 room, 40.12, 40.23). Long auto shots 2.17-7.02 and 21.20-26.10 checked by eye: the first hides one whip cut, the second is one continuous orbit plus a fade. 17.97 is a real jump cut (same framing, new clip). Audio: per-0.25 s loudness, band energies, spectral centroid and onset density with numpy (no listening possible).
